title: Relational Data Modeling
learning_outcomes: Explain what relational data modeling contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: one-to-one relationships.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. In this lesson, focus on one-to-one relationships; then compare it with one-to-many relationships. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use relational data modeling when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. For relational data modeling, begin with one-to-one relationships. Also distinguish one-to-many relationships; many-to-many relationships; junction tables. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Relational Data Modeling
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$sql = "SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE category = :category";
$params = [":category" => "books"];
echo str_contains($sql, ":category") && isset($params[":category"]) ? "named placeholder ready" : "check binding";

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, and transactions for changes that must succeed together.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for relational data modeling from top to bottom. Start by identifying one-to-one relationships, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.why: Input can change the meaning of a query.
common_mistakes.fix: Use PDO prepared statements and bind values separately from the query text.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming application checks are enough for data integrity.
common_mistakes.why: Concurrent requests can race and bypass check-then-write assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Use unique constraints, foreign keys, transactions, and appropriate locking.

common_mistakes.why: Memory and response time can grow unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Use filtering and bounded pagination or streaming for large results.

summary: Relational Data Modeling is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
